newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise with Latam, U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise with Latam, U.S. markets.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose on Thursday as gains in U.S. Treasuries and other Latin American markets offset the negative effects of the failure by Congress to reach quorum on government plans to raise fuel taxes.
The strong gains in U.S. markets after subdued wholesale inflation figures led the way for a turnaround of the initial decline of Argentine bonds on the Congress let-down.

Along with other Latin American markets, Argentine bonds got more mileage during the session from the approval in the Brazilian Senate of a bill authorizing the central bank to buy back Brady bonds and swap them for other sovereign paper.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.50 to 118.00. Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1-1/8 to 82.
"The whole region rose," said one trader. He said there was short-covering, caused partly by out-of-the money options positions in the market.
Traders reported busy trade through the session.
Even though the lower house of Congress did not reach a quorum on the government's tax measures, analysts said the market was not troubled by it since the measures are likely to pass next week.

Apart from that, there was positive news in Argentina's Senate approval of the extension of the key Fiscal Pact law, allowing the federal government to keep revenue from a proposed increase in fuel taxes without having to share it with the provinces. The passage of that law late on Wednesday means that when fuel tax rises eventually are passed, all the revenues will go to the central government.

Traders said the market was likely to look to the United States for direction again on Friday, with U.S. consumer price figures due for release. If the figures show subdued inflation, this session's strong move could well continue.
In the money markets, one day call money rates fell to 6.65 percent from 7.15 percent.
